name: Idi
catalog_citation: Schokkin, Dineke, Volker Gast, Nicholas Evans & Christian Döhler. 2021. Phonetics and phonology of Idi. In Kate L. Lindsey & Dineke Schokkin (eds.), Phonetic fieldwork in Southern New Guinea (Language Documentation & Conservation Special Publication 24), 76-1…
catalog_locator: Section 6 'Lack of stress and tone', p.103
catalog_quote: 6 Lack of stress and tone. Like other languages spoken in Southern New Guinea, Idi does not have tonal contrasts. Stress seems to be a marginal phenomenon in the language, if at all present, and there are no minimal pairs distinguished by just word-level stress.

audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated place (Schokkin et al. 2021, Section 6, p.103) in the held OA PDF. The source is a dedicated 2021 phonetics/phonology chapter by the primary fieldworkers and is the only phonology Glottolog lists for Idi; no reference grammar exists. The volume's overview (Evans 2021, p.7, held) independently states no distinctive stress in the sampled SNG languages except Urama, confirming the no-word-stress coding. The only unheld items (LT 2022 family overview, Evans et al. 2018 survey, an undated 21-pp anonymous sketch) are paywalled or unlocatable and are unlikely to overturn a first-hand 2021 statement; at most the LT paper could refine it.
